steps.cap: The wafer is coated with a thin film that changes wherever light touches it.
A stencil, called a mask, holds the pattern for one layer of the chip, drawn four times larger than life.
Light shines through the stencil, and a lens shrinks the image four times and lands it on the film.
A wash removes the film wherever the light landed, and the pattern is left on the wafer.
The machine steps across the wafer, printing one patch at a time, each about the size of a postage stamp.
